newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand's Finance One to restructure.
newsitem.headline: Thailand's Finance One to restructure.

text.p: Thailand's cash-strapped Finance One Plc said on Wednesday it would apply for a banking licence as part of a bold restructuring plan following the collapse of its much-vaunted merger with Thai Danu Bank Plc last week.

Company chairman Pin Chakkapak headed a panel of executives who told analysts the firm wanted to apply for a banking licence after a central bank-backed 8.28 billion baht ($318 million) rights issue in June brought in some much-needed cash.

The Thai financier, dubbed King Pin by local media for turning Finance One into Thailand's leading non-bank financial institution in the early 1990s, said his company would change its structure, seek new partners and shift its business focus.
The moves follow the breakdown of Finance One's planned merger with medium-sized Thai Danu Bank Plc last Friday.

The two firms announced plans to merge in late February in a move which authorities had hailed as a successful example of policies aimed at bolstering Thailand's troubled finance sector following a slide in asset values and revenues.
But the merger fell apart last week, dealing a blow to the government's credibility and casting doubts over Finance One's future, analysts said.
Finance One's declining asset quality and Thailand's overall liquidity crunch were seen as the main influences forcing the company to turn to Thai Danu for help.
But Wednesday's announcement showed that despite the firm's problems, Pin still plans to pursue a move into the retail banking sector, even without Thai Danu.

"With the present size and infrastructure of FIN1 group, FIN1 can form a consortium with other finance companies to apply for a banking licence from the Ministry of Finance and the Bank of Thailand," he told analysts.
Not all those attending the meeting were convinced.
"Personally I think the application for the banking licence is optimistic, and may depend on who subscribes to the capital increase," said an executive from Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi Ltd.

The central bank has guaranteed to buy new shares, but with Banque Paribas and Thai Farmers Bank Plc among Finance One's largest shareholders, it remains to be seen who will control the company after the share issue, analysts said.

They added that plans to separate the finance and securities arms of Finance One subsidiary Thana One Co Ltd and seek a foreign partner for its securities unit following the split could prove equally problematic.

"As far as I know the firm has no clear connection with an existing foreign securities house so it could prove difficult. I think it may depend on economic conditions improving," said a local analyst attending the briefing.
Thana One's finance operation will then focus on retail banking activities and become the sole consumer financier in the restructured group, Finance One executives said.
Finance One will return to its investment banking roots and move out of problematic consumer finance, executives said.
